title: Advanced Ratio and Proportion
tagline: Year 2 — Compound ratios, three-term ratios, ratio changes and componendo-dividendo

introduction.overview: Year 1 introduced the ratio of two quantities and simple sharing. Year 2 extends this to ratios of three or more quantities, compound and duplicate ratios, ratios that change when numbers are added or percentages applied, and ratios of mixtures. The common thread is turning every statement into "parts" and then working with one multiplier.
introduction.placementRelevance: Ratio problems are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds and are the base of partnership, mixture, age and salary questions. Two-condition ratio problems are a typical intermediate-level item.
introduction.realWorldContext: Sharing profit among partners, comparing salaries before and after a hike, and mixing paints or alloys in fixed proportions are everyday ratio problems.

learningObjectives: Combine two ratios into a three-term or four-term ratio
Use compound, duplicate and sub-duplicate ratios
Solve problems where a number is added to or removed from each term
Handle ratio changes caused by percentage increases
Apply componendo and dividendo and ratios of mixtures

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A ratio a : b means the quantities are ak and bk for some k. To compare or combine ratios, convert them to fractions and use the LCM to match the common term.

coreDefinitions: Continued ratio: a ratio of three or more terms such as a : b : c, obtained by matching the common term of a : b and b : c.
Compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd. Duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b². Sub-duplicate is √a : √b.
Inverse ratio of a : b is b : a.
Componendo: if a/b = c/d then (a+b)/b = (c+d)/d. Dividendo: (a−b)/b = (c−d)/d. Together: (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d).
Ratio of mixtures: when two mixtures with ratios a : b and c : d are combined in a given ratio, add the quantity of each ingredient separately.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Every ratio problem has the same engine: write each quantity as a multiple of one unknown k, form one equation from the extra information, solve for k and read off the answer. When two ratios share a middle term, scale them so that the middle term is the same number in both.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Think of ratios as recipes. 2 : 3 means 2 cups of A for 3 cups of B. Changing the batch size changes k, not the recipe. Adding the same amount to both ingredients changes the recipe, so the equation must be written with the added amount.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Combining ratios
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: a:b = p:q and b:c = r:s ⇒ a:b:c = pr : qr : qs
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Match the common term b by cross-multiplying.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Compound and duplicate
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Compound = ac : bd;  Duplicate = a² : b²;  Sub-duplicate = √a : √b

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Adding the same number
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: (a + x)/(b + x) = c/d → solve for x (or for k when a = pk, b = qk)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Percentage change in a ratio
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Multiply each term by its multiplier.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Componendo-dividendo
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Turns a hard equation into a simple one.

mainNarrative: To combine ratios, make the common term equal. For a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 5, the common term b is 4 in the first and 6 in the second. Scale the first by 3 (9 : 12) and the second by 2 (12 : 10), so a : b : c = 9 : 12 : 10.

When the same number is added to every term, you cannot add to the ratio; you must work with actual quantities. If A : B = 5 : 7 and adding 10 to each gives 3 : 4, write (5k + 10)/(7k + 10) = 3/4, so 20k + 40 = 21k + 30 and k = 10. A = 50, B = 70.
For percentage changes, convert each percentage to a multiplier. A salary ratio 3 : 5 where the first rises 20% and the second 10% becomes 3(1.2) : 5(1.1) = 3.6 : 5.5 = 36 : 55.

In mixture problems, find the amount of each ingredient in each part separately and then add. If vessel A has milk in 4/5 of its content and vessel B has 3/5, mixing them 2 : 3 gives milk (2×4/5 + 3×3/5)/5 = 17/25 of the mixture, so milk : water = 17 : 8.
Fractions in ratios, such as 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4, are cleared by multiplying by the LCM of the denominators (12): 6 : 4 : 3.

deepDiveAspects.title: Ratios and algebra
deepDiveAspects.content: Ratio statements are equations in disguise. "A is 2/3 of B and B is 1/4 of C" means A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 1 : 4, giving A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 12 after matching B.

deepDiveAspects.title: Checking answers
deepDiveAspects.content: Substitute back. If your numbers do not give the stated ratio after the change, the equation was set up wrongly.

problemVariations.typeName: Add or subtract from each term

solvedExamples.title: Three-term ratio
solvedExamples.question: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 5, find a : b : c.

steps.title: Scale the ratios
steps.explanation: a : b = 3 : 4 → multiply by 3 → 9 : 12. b : c = 6 : 5 → multiply by 2 → 12 : 10.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Scaling a ratio by a constant does not change its value.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Writing 3 : 4 : 5 by joining the ratios without matching b.

solvedExamples.title: Adding the same number
solvedExamples.question: The present ratio of two numbers is 5 : 7. If 10 is added to each, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. Find the numbers.

solvedExamples.title: Mixing two mixtures
solvedExamples.question: Vessel A has milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1 and vessel B in the ratio 3 : 2. The contents are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3 (A : B). Find the milk : water ratio in the mixture.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Add the milk and the water separately.

steps.title: Take 5 litres in all
steps.explanation: 2 L of A and 3 L of B.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Each vessel contributes in proportion to its share.

shortcutMethods.title: Common-term matching and multipliers

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Solve with simultaneous equations for every ratio problem.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Match common terms by LCM, use k for each quantity, and for percentage changes multiply by (1 ± r). Use componendo-dividendo to read x : y straight from (x+y)/(x−y).

rulesForApplication: Match the middle term using the LCM.
Clear fractions in a ratio by the LCM of denominators.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding to the ratio instead of to the quantities

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Scale so the middle term is the same.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Total of the ratio parts must divide the given total evenly; test options for this.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Attempt direct combining questions first; leave two-condition problems for later.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The same skill carries into partnership, mixtures and DI ratio questions.

summaryBullets: Match the common term to combine ratios.
Add to the quantities, not to the ratio.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I find a:b:c from two ratios?
Can I solve "add x to each term"?
Can I mix two mixtures by ratio?
